Odin × Godot

Box3D authoring contract

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Scene data and simulation ownershipIdentity and changesShapes and transformsRecovery and adaptersRequired evidenceUsing the surface

P5.1 builds on the bounded Gate B reference. The authoring surface serves one shared Box3D backend through separate Kit and Replay entry points. The P5.1 surface has Native Debug/Release/sanitizer, Odin and actual Godot SDK validation. Final author/export Gate C remains separate.

Scene data and simulation ownership#

Box3DWorld3D, Box3DBody3D and Box3DSensor3D describe initial content and presentation bindings. They do not step a native world automatically. Kit's Lane and Replay's Timeline remain the only tick owners. Scene nodes, Resources, instance IDs, native handles and process-local ownership tokens never enter canonical game state.

Before play, extract a detached definition from the scene and validate the whole candidate. Bake copied, immutable, versioned values in deterministic order. Native construction and each framework's attachment/checkpoint operation must either succeed completely or release the partial candidate. Source nodes and Resources can then be destroyed without invalidating owned bake data, geometry or recovery catalogs. Live owners still require their documented framework teardown.

Identity and changes#

Authored worlds, bodies and shape Resources have explicit stable keys. Durable IDs derive from a versioned namespace/key rule, not child order, array slots or native allocation order. Reordering unchanged content or saving/reloading it must preserve IDs. Duplicate keys, ID collisions and unresolved references are errors before publication; do not repair them by order-dependent probing. Content identity includes semantic geometry, poses, materials, filters and flags. Editing content changes compatibility identity while preserving the meaning of unchanged explicit keys. Logical authored IDs are64-bit values; Native catalog IDs are32-bit content-derived geometry IDs. Identical geometry shares one Native asset while retaining separate logical Resource identities. The exact schema1 fields are in API.md.

Shapes and transforms#

The surface includes box, sphere, capsule, convex hull, triangle mesh and heightfield Resources. A heightfield may bake to a deterministic triangle mesh. An offset or rotated box may bake to its exact convex vertices using the existing hull backend. Neither conversion permits dropping an authored transform or silently substituting different collision geometry.

Validate finite values, dimensions, unit rigid poses, scale policy, hull points, triangle indices and heightfield dimensions/counts with a field-specific error. Triangle meshes are currently static-only and cannot be sensors in the native binding; these combinations must be rejected explicitly. Do not approximate unsupported nonuniform analytic-shape scaling without a declared contract.

The existing bounded runtime profile is unchanged: at most35 bodies/shapes, 147 contacts, one hinge, eight catalog assets, H128, prediction/ordinary repair8 and64MiB tracked resource admission. Authoring validation must reject content that cannot fit; a new surface does not increase those limits.

Recovery and adapters#

The legacy primitive catalog retains recovery format1. Authored catalogs use the copied trusted V2 descriptor and recovery format2 for primitive, Hull and Mesh assets; heightfields bake to Mesh. Canonical bytes contain trusted asset references, never arbitrary geometry pointers. Full Mesh cache/manifold validation, native reconstruction/reencoding and failed-read atomicity remain required. The C/Odin V2 descriptor is72 bytes/align8 on supported64-bit targets, with actual C layout queries rather than assumed offsets.

Shared native construction owns the resulting world, trusted catalog and local stable-ID mapping. Kit consumes the world through its existing participant and network wrapper. Replay captures it through its existing complete checkpoint, provider and codec. Each adapter preserves its existing allocator, ownership, atomicity and tick contracts. Asset data is copied/retained before play; replay callbacks do not query the Godot scene or a mutable Resource.

Required evidence#

Completion needs stable-ID/order/collision/invalid-definition controls, actual construction and lifetime tests for every shape kind and sensors, complete canonical export/import and failed-read cleanup, both framework integrations, and actual Godot import plus .tres/.tscn save/reload and diagnostics. Ordinary SDK/module builds must preserve one verified shared Native image and natural cleanup. Gizmos/importer UX, characters/joints and the final author/export Gate C remain later P5 work.

Using the surface#

Copy addons/box3d_authoring into a project's addons/ directory. The optional editor plugin refreshes configuration warnings; the ordinary script classes and exported Resources do not need a custom Core extension. Add a Box3DWorld3D, give it an explicit stable_key namespace, and place Box3DBody3D/Box3DSensor3D descendants beneath it. Give each body a unique key and assign its shape Resources. Presentation node names are not durable IDs.

Resources expose stable_key, local_pose, positive scale, material/filter flags and their shape parameters. Capsule centers_a/centers_b are actual endpoints; heightfields are row-major Z then X with explicit grid spacing. Mesh/heightfield are Static, non-sensor and have sensor events disabled. The eight-asset limit counts deduplicated Native geometry, not logical Resource keys. Validation of that count belongs to the shared bake.

Call the Godot extractor once while the source is live:

Odin
import a "godot:box3d/authoring"
import ga "godot:box3d/godot/authoring"

scene, diagnostic := ga.extract(world_object, allocator)
defer ga.diagnostic_destroy(&diagnostic)
if diagnostic.error != .None {return}
defer a.destroy(&scene)

built, problem := a.build(&scene, profile_id)
defer a.built_destroy(&built)
if problem.error != .None {return}

The allocator must outlive its owning bake/maps; use the actual SDK context allocator for retained SDK owners. Destruction is checked and retryable when a real owner drop declines. An ordinary failed bake returns an empty output; failed build cleanup returns a surviving owner only when an actual drop declines, with an explicit diagnostic. Assignment aliases ownership.

For Kit, call kit/physics.authoring_attach with the built candidate, existing Instance/Lane, copied Side, tracked field declarations and ordinary ownership Config. Only the world transfers on success. The caller still owns the catalog and local maps. Use that catalog with the existing network_attach, then match network/provider/Lane teardown before releasing remaining authoring storage.

For Replay, replay/physics.authoring_config derives the value Config from the bake. authoring_checkpoint captures the borrowed built world with the trusted catalog through the existing provider. The checkpoint independently owns its image/catalog; use the same Config/catalog with network_codec_init and the normal Server/Client/Timeline or Godot Session APIs. No authoring object is a second tick owner. Copy only logical/native-independent keys into Game, not the local maps' live native handles.

The World can be detached from SceneTree during extraction. Relative poses come from local ancestry; scale/shear/reflection or top-level links are rejected without discarding them. Diagnostic paths use relative presentation names and remain available off-tree. Destroying source nodes/Resources after extraction does not invalidate copied bake data or subsequent Native construction.
